Definition: from δρέπω (to pluck); a gathering hook (especially for harvesting):--sickle.
BiblicalUsage: A sickle, the harvest tool, put in at once when the grain is ripe, and the sharp sickle of the angel who reaps the earth. The harvest of the earth is ripe, and the sickle falls on the vine of the earth as well as on the wheat.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the harvest is coming and the sickle is already in the angel's hand, which is why the sowing matters now. Every seed I sow is headed for a harvest, and I want mine to be wheat, not grapes of wrath.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
